source_artifacts.locator: agent card for payments-agent (as consumed by the orchestrator)

capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor skill, invoked with vendor bank details

inputs.source: Employee purchase request, manager-approved, SSO authenticated
Vendor quote emails and attachments, arriving from outside the company

instructions.note: 'Only pay vendors on the approved list' and 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' rely entirely on model instruction-following and on an unverified downstream assumption. There is no structural binding of the payment's bank details to the approved vendor's record, and runtime notes confirm payments-agent performs no such checks.

'Use the bank details from the chosen quote' directs the agent to take payment instructions directly from untrusted external vendor-quote email content, with no bound requiring cross-verification against a vendor system of record before those details drive an irreversible payment.

The instruction assumes payments-agent carries authority and responsibility for 'remaining checks' that it does not actually perform (runtime notes: payments-agent pays whatever bank details are in the task), creating a false sense of defense in depth.

elements.name: Manager approval record for the purchase request

controls.name: Manager approval of the purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval itself does not decay with model capability, but it occurs before the vendor is chosen or bank details exist, so it never reviews the actual payment destination. It does not function as a sink-level control for cap.delegate_payment regardless of model behavior; no residual credit is given for this finding.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement relies on the model matching the vendor name in the quote email to the approved list and refusing otherwise. It does not structurally verify the bank account/payment details against a vendor system of record, so a more capable or more persistently manipulated model can accept spoofed bank details attached to a nominally 'approved' vendor name.

controls.name: Signed or pinned agent card for payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: A pinned or signed card, checked on every connection rather than once at startup, would not decay with model capability and would close the impersonation path.

controls.name: Structural verification of payment bank details against a vendor system of record
controls.decay_rationale: If payments-agent (or the orchestrator) cross-checks bank details against a verified vendor master file outside the model's control before paying, this would not decay with model capability and would sever the path from untrusted quote content to actual payment destination.

findings.title: Authority laundering and instruction-only vendor check: untrusted vendor bank details flow to irreversible payment without re-approval (TC7)

attack_path.note: Untrusted external email supplies the vendor quote, including the bank payment details.
Vendor is checked against the approved list, but only by instruction, and apparently by name rather than bank account.
Approval is given before the quote exists; it covers item and budget only, never the final vendor or bank details.
Orchestrator delegates a payment task carrying the untrusted bank details to payments-agent.
Peer pays the bank details embedded in the task with no additional verification (runtime notes).

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string change in the orchestrator's config, or any observed instance of the agent accepting a vendor-name match despite inconsistent or unverifiable bank details.

evidence.observation: Orchestrator is instructed to pick the best quote and hand payments-agent 'the bank details from the chosen quote,' sourced from external vendor email, with no structural check against a verified vendor record.
Prompt states 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' diffusing responsibility to a peer that runtime notes confirm performs none.

The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists, so the approval cannot cover the vendor or bank details ultimately used for payment, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details embedded in the task with no further verification.
Vendor quotes, including the bank details ultimately used for payment, arrive by email from outside the company.

recommendations.action: Bind approval to the final payment details (verified vendor identity plus bank account), not just item and budget, and propagate a signed, verifiable approval token to payments-agent that it checks before paying.

Validate bank details against a system-of-record vendor database before payment; treat vendor quote email content as untrusted data that may suggest a vendor but must never directly supply payment instructions.
Replace the shared bearer-token trust between orchestrator and payments-agent with a bound, single-use authorization tied to the specific purchase/task id and verified destination.
Log and alert whenever a payment task's bank details differ from the approved vendor's stored bank details.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unpinned A2A connection to payments-agent enables impersonation of the payment-executing peer (ASI04/ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup, is not signed or pinned, and the connection has no mutual identity verification of payments-agent.
Payment task, including confidential bank/payment details, is sent to whatever endpoint the unverified card currently resolves to.

evidence.observation: The consumed agent card declares only a bearer authentication scheme used by the orchestrator to call payments-agent; nothing authenticates payments-agent's identity back to the orchestrator.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, so a compromised fetch (DNS, network, or distribution compromise) can substitute a different endpoint undetected.

payments-agent accepts any task carrying the orchestrator's bearer token with no per-task binding, so capturing or redirecting that channel is sufficient to intercept or redirect the irreversible payment capability and the confidential data within it.

recommendations.action: Pin or cryptographically sign the payments-agent agent card and verify it on every connection, not only at startup; reject unpinned or changed cards.
Require mutual authentication (mTLS or signed identity) between orchestrator and payments-agent instead of a static shared bearer token; scope tokens per task rather than per service.
Alert on any change to the resolved payments-agent endpoint or card hash between sessions.

rating.rationale: Two findings drive the rating. f2: the A2A connection to payments-agent has no peer identity verification, no pinning or signing of the agent card, and a shared bearer token blindly trusted for an irreversible, egress, delegate-class capability (cap.delegate_payment). No control of any kind currently mitigates this, so inherent and residual both sit at critical. f1: manager approval occurs before the vendor quote exists and its approval record is never passed to payments-agent, so the only effective preventive control on the path from untrusted vendor-quote bank details to payment is a behavioral, model-capability-dependent instruction ('only pay vendors on the approved list'), which is credited one tier of residual reduction from critical to high; under a model_upgrade trigger this instruction-dependent control is expected to fail per control_decay.md, returning the finding to critical. The forecast rating is therefore critical, driven jointly by f2's current lack of any structural control and f1's single point-of-failure dependent control.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of a deployed system.

No MCP/A2A client configuration, IaC, or source code was provided beyond the agent card JSON and narrative runtime notes; exact credential scoping and any bank-detail verification logic inside payments-agent are inferred from that narrative, which caps confidence at medium for finding f1.

No tool manifest for cap.vendor_list_read was provided; the approved-vendor check is assumed to be name-based matching without bank-account verification, consistent with the runtime notes' framing that payments-agent performs no additional checks.

autonomy.level was not explicitly declared by the design; it was inferred as A3_act_then_report because the only approval gate present does not cover the capability (cap.delegate_payment) that creates the risk, per rubric section 3.
